\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فقط} (faqat)}{فقط (faqat)}]{\fa{فقط} (faqat) — only}

\label{lesson:FA-C269-faqat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a street gutter, then the Persian for a pavement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فقط}}
\textbf{\fa{فقط}} — \emph{faqat} — \textquotedblleft{}only\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{faqat} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{faqaṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}only\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{q-ṭ-ṭ} (Lane). It is \emph{fa-}, \textquotedblleft{}so\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{qaṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}only, enough\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{faqat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{faqat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{faqat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a street gutter, then the Persian for a pavement, then say \emph{faqat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خوشبختانه} (khoshbakhtâne)}{خوشبختانه (khoshbakhtâne)}]{\fa{خوشبختانه} (khoshbakhtâne) — fortunately}

\label{lesson:FA-C269-khoshbakhtane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for completely, then the Persian for exactly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خوشبختانه}}
\textbf{\fa{خوشبختانه}} — \emph{khoshbakhtâne} — \textquotedblleft{}fortunately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khoshbakhtâne} is \emph{khosh}, \textquotedblleft{}good\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{bakht}, \textquotedblleft{}luck\textquotedblright{}, and the ending \emph{-âne}: by good luck. All are native; \emph{bakht} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{baxt}.
\end{cousinweb}
